Machine read · both lenses

Materials' 65-point lens gap signals earnings rebound

Materials' trailing P/E sits at the 89th percentile while its forward P/E is at the 23rd, a 65-point divergence—the widest in the table. That spread implies the market is pricing in a 127 percent earnings surge, an aggressive bet that recent margin compression is about to reverse sharply.

Consumer Staples' month-long de-rating hits extreme

Consumer Staples' forward percentile plunged 39 points in a month, the steepest decline among all sectors, yet its forward P/E of 19.11 remains near the middle of its five-year range. This suggests the market is rapidly repricing defensive growth lower, but the multiple has not yet caught up to the speed of the sentiment shift.

Real Estate's collapse belies stable earnings outlook

Real Estate's forward percentile dropped 49 points in a month to the 8th percentile, yet its implied earnings growth is only a 4 percent decline. The valuation compression appears driven by multiple de-rating rather than deteriorating fundamentals, leaving the sector priced for a downturn that earnings estimates do not yet reflect.

Written by deepseek-v4-flash-latest. Every figure is checked against the P/E tables; the reading of them is the model's and is not checked.

08

Are we expensive?

Three stacked panels on one time axis. Top: the ETF price (SPY or QQQ). Middle: its index's forward P/E against the 20th–80th percentile band of the trailing five years, plus a 200-day moving average. Bottom: forward earnings yield (1 ÷ forward P/E) next to the 10-year Treasury yield, with bars showing the spread — bars near zero mean stocks no longer offer much premium over bonds.

3 panels · shared Xas of 2026-09-25
09

Is the rally broad?

Top: SPY and QQQ, each rebased to 100 at the start of the visible window. Bottom: the share of S&P 500 stocks trading above their 50-day and 200-day moving averages. Watch for divergence. An index pushing to new highs while fewer of its stocks join in means a handful of large names carry the move.

Each dot is one trading day since 2006. Across: how far SPY stood below its 52-week high. Up: the share of S&P 500 stocks above their 200-day or 50-day average. The dotted box in the corner is the divergence from section 09, an index near its high with fewer than half its stocks joining in.
